topic: K1 Fix a bivariate positive-coefficient linear SCM with independent second-order regularly varying innovations, an arbitrary common body, local tail-index gap Delta_n, and intermediate sequence k_n; target the CTC direction contrast, not unrestricted causal direction. K2 derive the sharp joint local experiment and phase diagram across Delta_n log(n/k_n), Delta_n sqrt(k_n), and second-order bias. K3 construct adaptive threshold selection and an honest direction confidence set valid at equality and under either ordering. K4 prove matching contiguity and minimax lower bounds for unavoidable ambiguity. Use independent Pareto innovations and the anchor's climate and finance analyses as witness and consumers. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: At threshold u_n, the propagated-cause contribution ratio is C exp[-Delta_n log u_n], while tail-index differences have noise k_n^{-1/2}. Thus dominance changes on the log(n/k_n) scale and ordering detectability on the sqrt(k_n) scale, leaving a nonempty intermediate regime for polynomial k_n; generic tail-index LAN explains only the latter. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Derive the joint point-process experiment with uniform remainders when the local gap and second-order regular-variation bias reach their boundaries together. EARLY KILL TEST: For exact Pareto innovations, derive finite-threshold reverse CTC as a function of C u_n^{-Delta_n}; stop if no nonconstant limit remains when Delta_n log(n/k_n) tends to a finite constant.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive the joint local asymptotic experiment for the extremal marked point process, CTC direction contrast, and tail-index estimators when Delta_n log(n/k_n), Delta_n sqrt(k_n), and sqrt(k_n)A(n/k_n) are simultaneously bounded.

source_refs.claim: The CTC limit and inference theorems use fixed tail-index relations and gap-dependent rate restrictions on k, without local alternatives or a second-order-bias coordinate.
source_refs.author: Lisa Leimenstoll and Melanie Schienle

source_refs.claim: This paper proves LAN and semiparametric information bounds for a univariate tail index with a slowly varying nuisance, not for a causal mixture or CTC contrast.
source_refs.author: Jan Beirlant, Christel Bouquiaux, and Bas J. M. Werker
source_refs.venue: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference

source_refs.claim: Drees obtains Gaussian approximations, asymptotic bias, and normality for smooth tail functionals under weak second-order conditions, but not a locally colliding structural tail mixture.
source_refs.author: Holger Drees

source_refs.excerpt: The main theorem is open: it requires the centered rule-uniform lower bound, the reverse endpoint deficiency kernel
explicit marked rare-cell point-process limit plus the Gaussian behavior of common cells

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic tail-index LAN controls perturbations on the Delta_n sqrt(k_n) scale, whereas the structural mixture weight in reverse CTC changes on the distinct Delta_n log(n/k_n) scale and second-order bias adds the drift sqrt(k_n)A(n/k_n). The prior endpoint and weak-event proposals independently record that a count limit is insufficient without a marked process, a Gaussian common component, and reverse-deficiency control. For CTC, their rare-indicator reduction fails because an exceedance mark can come from either an innovation or its propagated copy, with a local intensity ratio. Existing fixed-regime CTC and univariate tail-process results therefore do not supply uniform likelihood remainders when all three coordinates reach their boundaries together.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A Le Cam convergence theorem to an explicit marked Poisson/Gaussian experiment with joint central sequence, drift, information operator, and uniform o_P(1) likelihood remainder over compact local-gap and second-order-bias coordinates.

writing_exemplar.why: Its fixed-regime identification-to-inference narrative is the closest motivation arc, while the new work sharpens the unresolved collision boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Heterogeneous tails change CTC identification -> finite-sample behavior depends sharply on the gap and threshold -> fixed-regime limits do not describe gaps approaching equality -> a joint local experiment must organize the competing scales

method_exemplars.technique: Embed Pareto-type tails in local submodels with a slowly varying nuisance, expand log likelihoods, and identify LAN information and convolution bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the tail-index-score coordinate of the desired experiment; the new proof must add causal-mixture and second-order-bias coordinates.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a Gaussian approximation to the empirical tail-quantile process and a functional delta method retaining explicit second-order bias.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The CTC and Hill components become coupled functionals of one tail process after the local two-innovation mixture is retained.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish weak convergence and multiplier-bootstrap consistency for empirical tail-copula processes under nonrestrictive smoothness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: CTC is an integral functional of a survival-tail process, so this machinery is the closest route to the joint rank-process coordinate and feasible inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the finite-threshold reverse CTC transition in the bivariate positive-coefficient linear SCM when Delta_n log u_n is bounded, including the exact-Pareto curve as a function of C u_n^{-Delta_n} and a uniform second-order expansion.

source_refs.claim: The paper gives pointwise limiting CTC values for fixed equal or unequal tail indices and documents slow, tail-family-dependent convergence for close indices, but no local finite-threshold transition.
source_refs.author: Lisa Leimenstoll and Melanie Schienle

source_refs.claim: The foundational CTC paper derives population identification and consistency under comparable regularly varying tails, using asymptotic rather than local finite-threshold formulas.
source_refs.author: Nicola Gnecco, Nicolai Meinshausen, Jonas Peters, and Sebastian Engelke

open_problems.why_unsolved: The dominant-tail sum approximation used for fixed unequal indices discards the lighter innovation before evaluating the CTC rank functional. That step is non-uniform when Delta_n log u_n stays bounded: both innovation mechanisms retain order-one conditional mixture weights, and the arbitrary common body can still enter the response rank. The scan found fixed-regime CTC limits and finite-sample simulations, but no local transition indexed by C u^{-Delta}. The first proof step that must change is the one-big-jump/dominant-tail reduction, replacing it with a two-component conditional exceedance mixture uniform in the local gap.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A closed-form exact-Pareto reverse-CTC function g(C u_n^{-Delta_n}, beta, alpha), its endpoint limits, and a uniform remainder theorem over bounded Delta_n log u_n and second-order regular-variation neighborhoods.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames heterogeneous tails as both an identification resource and a source of finite-sample failure, with climate and finance consumers matching the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CTC identifies causal propagation in extremes -> heterogeneous tail ordering changes population CTC -> close indices converge slowly and direction decisions become unstable -> a local finite-threshold CTC transition is needed

method_exemplars.technique: Condition on the innovation responsible for an extreme and evaluate the induced rank functional to obtain the asymmetric CTC formula.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired transition keeps the same innovation-mixture identification argument but retains both tail contributions instead of taking a fixed-gap dominant-tail limit.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent empirical CTC through the empirical survival copula and derive its root-k limit law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the local population transition is known, the same rank-based estimator is the natural statistic whose centering and limit law must be uniform along it.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a data-driven threshold selector and an honest set-valued confidence procedure for the CTC direction contrast that is uniformly valid at equal tail indices and under either local ordering over second-order regularly varying innovations.

source_refs.claim: The paper calls k crucial, selects it using an independent simulation study, and reports weak tail-index-pretest discrimination for close indices and deterioration in more complex causal configurations.
source_refs.author: Lisa Leimenstoll and Melanie Schienle

source_refs.claim: This paper constructs honest adaptive confidence intervals for a univariate tail coefficient over second-order Pareto classes and proves an almost matching lower bound.
source_refs.author: Alexandra Carpentier and Arlene K. H. Kim

source_refs.claim: The paper proves a lower bound on uniformly valid tail-index interval length and constructs honest intervals incorporating worst-case tail-approximation bias.
source_refs.author: Yuya Sasaki and Yulong Wang

source_refs.excerpt: The Poisson upper half was dropped, leaving only a lower obstruction.
Build the adaptive calibration from a joint marked process for every score-bearing A,Y cell

open_problems.why_unsolved: The admissible growth of k in CTC theory depends on the unknown tail-index gap, while bias depends on unknown second-order behavior. Selecting k and then pretesting equality is nonregular at Delta=0: close gaps affect population CTC on the logarithmic scale but a tail-index pretest resolves them only on the root-k scale. The prior weak-event run separately records that its finite-effective-count upper calibration was dropped and prescribes joint marked-process calibration. Existing honest tail-index intervals control a scalar marginal target, not a coupled rank-based CTC contrast after data-driven threshold selection or a set-valued direction decision under both orderings.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit selector k_hat and confidence set taking values in {forward, reverse, ambiguous} with uniform 1-alpha coverage over the stated second-order model and an adaptive diameter or ambiguity-probability guarantee matching oracle behavior away from equality.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly motivates CTC direction inference, documents threshold sensitivity, and supplies climate and finance cases where an honest ambiguity report matters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CTC direction tests matter in climate and finance -> validity depends on tail ordering and k -> close indices and simulation-chosen thresholds destabilize decisions -> honest adaptive direction confidence sets are required

method_exemplars.technique: Derive a uniform distributional approximation and inflate the interval by a worst-case nonparametric tail-bias bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The CTC direction set likewise needs uniform coverage under unknown second-order bias, but for a bivariate causal contrast at an ordering boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate honest adaptation into testing the second-order class, construct a uniform adaptive interval, and pair it with a minimax lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its testing-based architecture can be ported from a scalar tail coefficient to the nuisance class governing the CTC threshold and direction set.

method_exemplars.technique: Choose k by validation over a sparse grid using explicit variance comparisons, with nonasymptotic guarantees under regular variation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the closest calibration-light adaptive-threshold device; the new proof must couple its stability comparisons to bivariate CTC instead of one Hill estimate.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the minimax probability of resolving the CTC direction contrast over local tail-index collisions by constructing opposite-direction contiguous SCM sequences and matching the lower bound with an attainable ambiguity frontier.

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that fixed tail ordering can identify or erase CTC asymmetry and that close gaps converge slowly, but gives no contiguity or minimax lower bound for direction decisions.
source_refs.author: Lisa Leimenstoll and Melanie Schienle

source_refs.claim: LAN submodels yield semiparametric variance lower bounds for tail-index estimation, but the decision parameter is a scalar tail index rather than causal direction.
source_refs.author: Jan Beirlant, Christel Bouquiaux, and Bas J. M. Werker
source_refs.venue: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference

source_refs.claim: Novak gives nonasymptotic minimax lower bounds for tail-index, tail-constant, and extreme-quantile inference over heavy-tail classes, not observationally close opposite causal structures.
source_refs.author: S. Y. Novak

source_refs.excerpt: the three-cell Bernoulli least-favorable family with V/r = a + a^2(1-4r) in [3/16, 21/16]
Finite-sample inference on a restricted domain, dependent-latent robustness, and direct-effect identification.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing lower bounds perturb a marginal heavy-tail law or scalar tail index. A direction converse instead needs two positive-coefficient SCMs with opposite causal orders and different innovation tails whose observational extreme processes have bounded likelihood ratio while their CTC contrasts differ. The prior weak-event witness varies only a rare Bernoulli cell, and the LiNGAM proposal supplies population orientation geometry but leaves finite-sample direction inference open. Its product-binomial divergence calculation must be replaced by Hellinger or likelihood control for marked tail processes while preserving innovation independence, an arbitrary common body, both orderings, and simultaneous logarithmic, root-k, and second-order nuisance paths.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit pair or mixture of forward and reverse SCM arrays with a limiting likelihood ratio or bounded Hellinger/KL distance, yielding a minimax direction-error lower envelope and confidence-set ambiguity bound attained in each phase by a CTC procedure.

writing_exemplar.why: Its identification table naturally motivates asking where pointwise CTC differences cease to be statistically resolvable.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Tail ordering changes population CTC identification -> close orderings generate nearly indistinguishable samples -> pointwise consistency does not quantify unavoidable error -> minimax contiguity must delineate the ambiguity region

method_exemplars.technique: Map innovation ancestry and tail contributions into a directional CTC contrast.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The lower-bound alternatives must make this causal contrast change sign while their induced observational tail laws remain close.

method_exemplars.technique: Use LAN submodels and Le Cam testing arguments to turn likelihood expansions into information lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies contiguity machinery, but the submodel must be rebuilt for two opposite SCM directions and the CTC mark process.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct nearby heavy-tail distributions with controlled testing distance to obtain finite-sample minimax probability lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its two-point method can be adapted once opposite-direction SCM laws with controlled distance and separated CTC contrasts are available.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp adaptation price for selecting the CTC exceedance threshold when both the tail-index gap and the second-order regular-variation class are unknown.

source_refs.excerpt: remain honest after a climate threshold or projection is selected to maximize causal evidence?
A tail-index-adaptive causal WCP oracle inequality, or a matching adaptation penalty, over gamma in (1,2).

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two prior proposals isolate complementary selection pathologies: choosing a climate threshold to strengthen causal evidence invalidates fixed-threshold calibration, while adaptation to an unknown tail class can impose a nonzero penalty. In CTC the oracle balance is three-way among k_n^{-1/2} noise, A(n/k_n) bias, and exp{-Delta_n log(n/k_n)} directional dilution, so ordinary bias-variance selection can favor an apparent direction. The first proof step that changes from scalar tail adaptation is replacing a fixed-threshold score bound with a simultaneous tail empirical-process and bias envelope over nested candidate thresholds, including their dependence and a local structural-mixture coordinate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An oracle inequality for a concrete multiscale threshold selector and uniformly honest CTC confidence set, plus a matching lower bound identifying any logarithmic or other adaptation penalty over stated second-order classes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing directly connects unknown second-order tail behavior, honest adaptation, and an almost matching impossibility result; the destination swaps the scalar tail coefficient for CTC direction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Tail procedures need a threshold -> the oracle threshold depends on unknown second-order regularity -> honest adaptation incurs a testing problem and possible penalty -> quantify that price for the CTC direction contrast

method_exemplars.technique: Use between-class moduli and two-point expected-length arguments to prove unavoidable confidence-interval adaptation costs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The CTC result must compare honest diameter over nested second-order tail classes whose oracle thresholds differ.

method_exemplars.technique: Validate Hill estimators over a sparse threshold grid using variance comparisons and prove near-minimax adaptive behavior under regular variation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its multiscale selector supplies the upper-bound architecture, while CTC adds nested bivariate ranks and direction dilution to the comparison process.

literature_map:
1. Gnecco, Meinshausen, Peters, and Engelke (2021, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1908.05097) introduce CTC, prove population causal-order recovery under comparable tails, and give a consistent rank estimator.
2. Their different-tail discussion is pointwise; the finance application already shows threshold sensitivity and loss of asymmetry when ancestor and descendant tails differ.
3. Pasche, Chavez-Demoulin, and Davison (2023, Extremes, doi:10.1007/s10687-022-00456-4) add GPD-based confounder adjustment and a permutation test, while retaining threshold and finite-sample bias issues.
4. Leimenstoll and Schienle (2026, arXiv:2608.22957) are the closest anchor: heterogeneous innovation tails, CTC direction/confounder tests, and climate plus S&P 500-Bitcoin applications.
5. Their fixed-ordering theory makes reverse CTC equal one-half, an interior value, or one depending on the tail-index relation; it does not resolve local collisions.
6. Their rate restrictions on k tighten as the gap closes, simulations need much larger n for close indices, and Student-t convergence is slower than Pareto convergence.
7. Their practical k comes from a separate simulation study, while the tail-index pretest weakly discriminates close indices and can deteriorate under confounding.
8. Beirlant, Bouquiaux, and Werker (2006, JSP&I, doi:10.1016/j.jspi.2004.08.018) provide univariate tail-index LAN and information bounds, explaining only the root-k local scale.
9. Drees (1998, Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, doi:10.1111/1467-9469.00097) supplies empirical-tail-quantile Gaussian approximation and explicit second-order bias for smooth tail functionals.
10. Buecher and Dette (2013, Bernoulli, arXiv:1102.0110) give weak convergence and multiplier bootstrap for empirical tail-copula processes, the closest inference machinery for rank-based CTC.
11. Carpentier and Kim (2014 EJS; 2015 Statistica Sinica, arXiv:1312.2968 and 1309.2585) establish honest/adaptive tail-index inference and unavoidable adaptation losses over second-order Pareto classes.
12. Sasaki and Wang (2024, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2210.05074) show honest tail-index intervals must incorporate worst-case bias, warning against naive post-threshold CTC intervals.
13. Lederer, Sabourin, and Taheri (2025, arXiv:2505.22371) give calibration-light adaptive k selection for Hill estimation, but not for a bivariate causal contrast or equality boundary.
14. Novak (2014, Bernoulli, arXiv:1403.3278) and Beirlant et al. provide heavy-tail minimax tools, yet no located paper constructs contiguous opposite-direction SCMs or a CTC ambiguity lower bound.
15. The live opportunity is the collision of a logarithmic structural-mixture scale, a root-k tail-index scale, and second-order bias, followed by adaptive honest inference and matching direction lower bounds.
prior_proposal_map:
1. The current stat_ctc_tailindex_collision_frontier directory contains only state, pipeline, logs, and an orchestrator decision log; no proposal core or reviewer JSON exists yet.
2. The closest inference predecessor is downgraded stat_pn_weak_event_honest_inference/poisson_gaussian_diameter_frontier, including all three rejected proposal angles and reviews through angle3_v5.
3. Its README records that the promised Poisson-calibrated upper procedure was dropped, while its three-cell Bernoulli least-favorable family remains reusable for lower bounds.
4. Its reviewers repeatedly prescribed an explicit marked rare-cell point process, adaptive finite-count calibration, and a phase split among bounded-count, learner-limited, and Gaussian regimes.
5. Its rejected-angle OEQ on threshold-selected climate evidence supplies the direct post-selection-honesty analogue for adaptive CTC threshold choice.
6. Active exp_two_wave_endpoint_poisson_minimax was mined for its pair-thinning Poisson experiment, reverse-deficiency boundary, marked-process classification, and uniform nine-cell exhaustion; reviews angle0_v1-v6 and angle1_v1-v2 were inspected.
7. Downgraded stat_conformal_overlap_frontier_v1 and all four rejected proto cores were inspected for the explicitly banked tail-index-adaptation-penalty direction.
8. Accepted eid_lingam_direction_min_order_v1/truncated_cumulant_minimality, its three rejected proposal TeX files, proto-core archive, and reviews were inspected as the nearest structural-direction run; it leaves finite-sample inference open but is less tail-specific.
